questions.question: In the classic five-phase model of hacking taught in ethical hacking courses, which phase immediately follows gaining access?
questions.domain: Information Security and Ethical Hacking Overview

citations.source: EC-Council CEH Exam Blueprint v5.0 / CEH v13 brochure
citations.reference: M01 Introduction to Ethical Hacking (Information Security and Ethical Hacking Overview)

options.text: Maintaining access
Scanning
Reconnaissance
Clearing tracks

questions.justification: Correct Answer: A. The five phases are reconnaissance, scanning, gaining access, maintaining access and clearing tracks. Once an attacker has a foothold, the next goal is to keep it, for example through persistence mechanisms, which is the maintaining access phase. Scanning happens before access is gained, when the attacker probes live hosts, ports and services. Reconnaissance is the very first phase, focused on gathering information about the target. Clearing tracks is the final phase, in which the attacker tries to erase evidence after access has already been established and maintained.

questions.question: A company introduces a mandatory annual security awareness training program for all employees. Into which category of information security controls does this program fall?
questions.domain: Information Security and Ethical Hacking Overview

citations.source: EC-Council CEH Exam Blueprint v5.0 / CEH v13 brochure
citations.reference: M01 Introduction to Ethical Hacking (Information Security and Ethical Hacking Overview)

options.text: Physical control
Administrative control
Technical control
Compensating technical safeguard

questions.justification: Correct Answer: B. Security controls are commonly grouped as administrative, technical and physical. Training programs, policies, procedures and awareness campaigns are administrative (managerial) controls because they shape human behavior through governance rather than technology. A technical control is implemented in hardware or software, such as a firewall, encryption or an access control list. A physical control protects the facility or equipment, such as locks, guards and fences. A compensating technical safeguard is an alternative technology used when a primary control cannot be applied, which does not describe a training program.

questions.question: Threat intelligence shows that an adversary combined a malicious macro with a legitimate-looking invoice document, creating a deliverable package, but had not yet sent it to anyone. Which Cyber Kill Chain stage does this activity represent?
questions.domain: Information Security and Ethical Hacking Overview

citations.source: EC-Council CEH Exam Blueprint v5.0 / CEH v13 brochure
citations.reference: M01 Introduction to Ethical Hacking (Information Security and Ethical Hacking Overview)

options.text: Delivery
Weaponization
Installation
Exploitation

questions.justification: Correct Answer: B. In the Lockheed Martin Cyber Kill Chain, weaponization is the stage in which the adversary couples an exploit or malicious code with a deliverable payload, such as a document, before transmitting it. Delivery would begin only when the package is actually transmitted to the victim, for example by email or a USB drive. Exploitation occurs when the malicious code is triggered on the victim system. Installation refers to placing a persistent backdoor or implant on the compromised host. Since nothing has been sent yet, the activity is weaponization.

questions.question: While analyzing an intrusion with the Diamond Model of Intrusion Analysis, an analyst records the domain names and IP addresses the attacker used to deliver malware and maintain command and control. Which core feature of the model do these indicators describe?
questions.domain: Information Security and Ethical Hacking Overview

citations.source: EC-Council CEH Exam Blueprint v5.0 / CEH v13 brochure
citations.reference: M01 Introduction to Ethical Hacking (Information Security and Ethical Hacking Overview)

options.text: Victim
Adversary
Infrastructure
Capability

questions.justification: Correct Answer: C. The Diamond Model has four core features: adversary, capability, infrastructure and victim. Infrastructure is the physical or logical communication structure the adversary uses to deliver capabilities and maintain control, such as IP addresses, domains and email accounts. Capability refers to the tools and techniques used, such as the malware itself or an exploit. Adversary is the actor or organization responsible for the intrusion. Victim is the targeted organization, person or asset. Domains and IP addresses used for delivery and command and control therefore map to infrastructure.

questions.question: During an authorized penetration test, a tester realizes that an IP address listed in scope actually belongs to shared infrastructure operated by a third-party hosting provider, not by the client. What is the most appropriate course of action?
questions.domain: Information Security and Ethical Hacking Overview

citations.source: EC-Council CEH Exam Blueprint v5.0 / CEH v13 brochure
citations.reference: M01 Introduction to Ethical Hacking (Information Security and Ethical Hacking Overview)

options.text: Exclude the asset silently and omit the finding from the final report
Test the asset only with low-intensity techniques to limit any impact
Pause testing that asset and confirm authorization with the client and the provider
Continue testing, because the address appears in the signed scope document

questions.justification: Correct Answer: C. Authorization must come from the party that owns or legally controls the asset. A client cannot grant permission to test infrastructure it does not own, so the tester should pause and obtain confirmation, respecting the provider's testing policy. Continuing simply because the address appears in the scope document risks unauthorized access, since the scope itself was wrong. Using low-intensity techniques does not change the legal status of unauthorized testing. Silently excluding the asset and omitting it from the report hides a scoping error the client needs to know about and breaks transparency.

questions.question: Which of the following activities is an example of passive footprinting?

citations.source: EC-Council CEH Exam Blueprint v5.0 / CEH v13 brochure
citations.reference: M02 Footprinting and Reconnaissance (Reconnaissance Techniques)

options.text: Probing the target's mail server for open ports
Calling the help desk while pretending to be a new employee
Reviewing archived versions of the target's website on a public web archive
Sending ICMP echo requests to the target's address range

questions.justification: Correct Answer: C. Passive footprinting gathers information without directly interacting with the target's systems, so the target has little or no chance of noticing it. Reviewing historical copies of a website stored by a public archive uses third-party data only. Sending ICMP echo requests directly touches the target's hosts, making it active host discovery. Calling the help desk under a false identity is active social engineering that involves direct contact with staff. Probing a mail server for open ports is active scanning, which generates traffic that the target can log and detect.

questions.question: Which type of information is typically revealed by a Whois lookup on an organization's domain name?

citations.source: EC-Council CEH Exam Blueprint v5.0 / CEH v13 brochure
citations.reference: M02 Footprinting and Reconnaissance (Reconnaissance Techniques)

options.text: Patch levels of the organization's workstations
Internal usernames stored in the corporate directory
Open ports and running service versions on the web server
Registrar, key dates, name servers and registrant contacts

questions.justification: Correct Answer: D. Whois databases maintained by registries and registrars hold domain registration records: the registrar, creation and expiry dates, authoritative name servers and, unless privacy services are used, registrant and technical contacts. This makes Whois a key passive footprinting source. Open ports and service versions are discovered through scanning and banner grabbing, not registration records. Internal directory usernames are obtained through enumeration of services such as LDAP or SMB. Workstation patch levels require vulnerability assessment of the hosts themselves and never appear in domain registration data.

questions.question: An audit finds that the organization's authoritative DNS server returns a complete copy of its zone data to any host that requests it. Which countermeasure directly addresses this exposure?

citations.source: EC-Council CEH Exam Blueprint v5.0 / CEH v13 brochure
citations.reference: M02 Footprinting and Reconnaissance (Reconnaissance Techniques)

options.text: Restrict zone transfers to authorized secondary name servers only
Sign the zone with DNSSEC so records cannot be forged
Increase the TTL of all records to reduce query volume
Disable recursive queries for external clients

questions.justification: Correct Answer: A. Unrestricted zone transfers let anyone download every hostname and address in the zone, giving attackers a ready-made network map. Limiting transfers to known secondary servers, ideally with transaction signatures, closes this exposure. DNSSEC protects the integrity and authenticity of records but does not stop someone from receiving the full zone. Raising TTL values only affects caching duration and has no effect on who can request a transfer. Disabling external recursion is good practice against cache abuse and amplification, but an authoritative zone transfer is a separate function that remains open.

questions.question: A security team discovers that confidential internal spreadsheets are indexed by public search engines because they were stored in a publicly reachable web directory. Which action provides the most effective long-term protection?

citations.source: EC-Council CEH Exam Blueprint v5.0 / CEH v13 brochure
citations.reference: M02 Footprinting and Reconnaissance (Reconnaissance Techniques)

options.text: Remove the files, enforce access controls and request removal from search indexes
Move the web server behind a load balancer with a new public IP address
Rename the files with random names so they are harder to guess
List the sensitive directory in robots.txt so that search engine crawlers skip it in the future

questions.justification: Correct Answer: A. The root cause is sensitive content exposed on a public server, so it must be removed or protected by authentication, and cached copies should be purged from search engines. A robots.txt entry is only a voluntary request to well-behaved crawlers; it does not restrict access and actually advertises the location of sensitive directories to anyone reading the file. Random file names are security through obscurity and fail once a link leaks. A load balancer or new IP address changes nothing about who can reach the content.

questions.question: Attackers have been building detailed target lists of a company's administrators using public professional networking profiles that describe internal technologies and reporting lines. Which countermeasure best reduces this footprinting exposure?

citations.source: EC-Council CEH Exam Blueprint v5.0 / CEH v13 brochure
citations.reference: M02 Footprinting and Reconnaissance (Reconnaissance Techniques)

options.text: Block social networking sites at the corporate web proxy for all users
Require encryption for all outbound corporate email
A disclosure policy for employees, reinforced by awareness training
Deploy a network intrusion detection system at the perimeter

questions.justification: Correct Answer: C. The information is published voluntarily by employees on third-party platforms, so the effective control is governing what staff disclose about roles, internal systems and technologies, supported by awareness training that explains how attackers use such data. Blocking social sites at the proxy does nothing about profiles updated from personal devices and already visible to the public. A network IDS cannot see OSINT gathering that happens entirely on external websites. Email encryption protects message confidentiality in transit but does not address information employees post publicly.

questions.question: What is the primary goal of host discovery during the network scanning phase?

citations.source: EC-Council CEH Exam Blueprint v5.0 / CEH v13 brochure
citations.reference: M03 Scanning Networks (Reconnaissance Techniques)

options.text: Recovering plaintext passwords from captured network traffic
Determining which IP addresses in a range correspond to live systems
Identifying the exact software version behind each open port
Rating discovered weaknesses by severity for the final report

questions.justification: Correct Answer: B. Host discovery is the first step of scanning: it narrows a large address range down to the systems that are actually online, so that later steps focus only on live targets. Identifying software versions is service version detection or banner grabbing, performed after live hosts and open ports are known. Recovering passwords from traffic is sniffing or credential attack activity, not scanning. Rating weaknesses by severity belongs to vulnerability analysis and reporting, which happen after the network has been mapped.

questions.question: Which sequence correctly describes the TCP three-way handshake used to establish a connection?

citations.source: EC-Council CEH Exam Blueprint v5.0 / CEH v13 brochure
citations.reference: M03 Scanning Networks (Reconnaissance Techniques)

options.text: SYN, RST, ACK
SYN, ACK, FIN
ACK, SYN, SYN-ACK
SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK

questions.justification: Correct Answer: D. A TCP connection starts with the client sending a SYN, the server answering with SYN-ACK to acknowledge and synchronize its own sequence number, and the client completing the process with an ACK. Understanding this exchange is essential for interpreting scan types and their detection. The sequence ending in FIN is wrong because FIN is used to close connections, not open them. Starting with an ACK reverses the logical order of synchronization. A sequence containing RST describes a reset, which aborts a connection rather than establishing one.

questions.question: A scan technique sends a SYN packet and, when a SYN-ACK is received, replies with RST instead of completing the connection. What is this technique commonly called?

citations.source: EC-Council CEH Exam Blueprint v5.0 / CEH v13 brochure
citations.reference: M03 Scanning Networks (Reconnaissance Techniques)

options.text: Xmas scan
Half-open (stealth) scan
Full TCP connect scan
Idle (zombie) scan

questions.justification: Correct Answer: B. Because the handshake is never completed, this technique is known as a half-open or stealth scan; historically, some applications did not log incomplete connections. Defenders detect it by monitoring for many SYNs followed by resets. A full TCP connect scan completes the entire three-way handshake, so the connection is established and more likely to be logged. An idle scan relies on a third-party host with predictable IP identifiers to hide the scanner's address. An Xmas scan sends packets with the FIN, PSH and URG flags set, not a SYN.

questions.question: A web server responds to every request with a header that discloses the exact product name and version. Which countermeasure best reduces the value of this information to an attacker performing OS and service fingerprinting?

citations.source: EC-Council CEH Exam Blueprint v5.0 / CEH v13 brochure
citations.reference: M03 Scanning Networks (Reconnaissance Techniques)

options.text: Increase the verbosity of the web server's access logs
Allow ICMP echo requests so monitoring tools can confirm availability
Place the web server behind network address translation
Suppress or customize service banners so they do not reveal product and version details

questions.justification: Correct Answer: D. Banner grabbing relies on services announcing their product and version, which lets attackers match the target against known vulnerabilities. Disabling or altering banners, together with timely patching, reduces that value. Allowing ICMP echo requests makes host discovery easier and does nothing to hide version details. NAT hides internal addressing but still forwards requests to the server, which continues to send the revealing header. Verbose logging helps detection and forensics after the fact, but does not stop the information from being disclosed in every response.

questions.question: A defender suspects that scans are evading the network IDS by splitting probe headers across many tiny IP fragments. Which configuration change most directly counters this evasion technique?

citations.source: EC-Council CEH Exam Blueprint v5.0 / CEH v13 brochure
citations.reference: M03 Scanning Networks (Reconnaissance Techniques)

options.text: Enable fragment reassembly on the IDS before inspection
Increase the IDS signature update frequency to hourly
Move the IDS sensor to a mirror port on the internal switch
Configure the IDS to inspect only the first fragment of each packet

questions.justification: Correct Answer: A. Fragmentation evasion works when the sensor inspects fragments individually and never sees the complete header or payload. Reassembling fragments before inspection, as the destination host would, lets signatures match the whole packet; overlapping or tiny fragments can also be flagged or dropped. Updating signatures more often does not help when the engine cannot see the reconstructed packet. Inspecting only the first fragment is precisely the weakness being exploited. Relocating the sensor to a mirror port changes what traffic is visible but not how fragments are handled.
questions.review_notes: AI-authored original question pending SME review.

questions.question: Which statement best describes enumeration in the ethical hacking methodology?

citations.source: EC-Council CEH Exam Blueprint v5.0 / CEH v13 brochure
citations.reference: M04 Enumeration (Reconnaissance Techniques)

options.text: Actively connecting to systems to extract user names, shares, groups and services
Exploiting a vulnerability to execute code on a target host
Removing log entries to hide activity after a compromise
Collecting publicly available information without touching the target's systems

questions.justification: Correct Answer: A. Enumeration follows scanning and involves actively connecting to target systems and querying services to extract detailed information such as account names, machine names, network shares, groups and service configurations. It is typically performed from an intranet-like position and is more intrusive than scanning. Collecting public information without touching the target is passive footprinting. Exploiting a vulnerability to run code belongs to the gaining access phase of system hacking. Removing log entries is part of clearing tracks, the final phase of the hacking methodology.

questions.question: An assessment finds network devices running SNMPv1 with the default community strings still configured. Which countermeasure most effectively reduces the risk of SNMP enumeration?

citations.source: EC-Council CEH Exam Blueprint v5.0 / CEH v13 brochure
citations.reference: M04 Enumeration (Reconnaissance Techniques)

options.text: Downgrade the devices to SNMPv1 read-only mode for compatibility
Rely on NAT at the perimeter to hide the devices' SNMP service from outsiders
Enable SNMP on every interface to improve monitoring coverage
Move to SNMPv3 with authentication and encryption and remove default strings

questions.justification: Correct Answer: D. Default community strings act as well-known passwords, letting anyone query device information such as interfaces, routing tables and accounts. SNMPv3 adds user-based authentication and encryption, and removing defaults eliminates the easiest path; limiting SNMP access to management hosts helps further. Read-only SNMPv1 still exposes all readable data with a guessable string in cleartext. Enabling SNMP on more interfaces increases the attack surface. NAT does not protect against internal attackers and is not an access control for the service itself.
questions.review_notes: AI-authored original question pending SME review.

questions.question: A mail server confirms whether a given mailbox exists when asked with certain protocol commands, allowing attackers to build a list of valid user accounts. Which countermeasure addresses this SMTP enumeration risk?

citations.source: EC-Council CEH Exam Blueprint v5.0 / CEH v13 brochure
citations.reference: M04 Enumeration (Reconnaissance Techniques)

options.text: Enable open relay so responses look identical for all recipients
Move the SMTP service to a non-standard TCP port
Disable VRFY and EXPN and return generic responses for unknown recipients
Enable STARTTLS so that all SMTP sessions with the server are encrypted

questions.justification: Correct Answer: C. SMTP verbs such as VRFY and EXPN, and distinguishable responses to recipient checks, disclose which accounts or mailing lists exist. Disabling these verbs and returning uniform responses removes that oracle. Enabling an open relay is a serious misconfiguration that allows spam and abuse, and does not stop enumeration. Moving to a non-standard port is obscurity; the service is easily found by scanning. STARTTLS encrypts the session in transit, but the server still answers the enumeration queries, just over an encrypted channel.
questions.review_notes: AI-authored original question pending SME review.

questions.question: A directory server allows anonymous binds, so unauthenticated clients can query user objects and group memberships. Which change most directly prevents this LDAP enumeration?

citations.source: EC-Council CEH Exam Blueprint v5.0 / CEH v13 brochure
citations.reference: M04 Enumeration (Reconnaissance Techniques)

options.text: Move the directory service to the LDAPS port and keep the current bind settings
Replicate the directory to an additional domain controller
Increase the directory's query timeout to slow large searches
Disable anonymous binds and require authenticated access with least-privilege read permissions

questions.justification: Correct Answer: D. The problem is that the directory answers queries without authentication. Requiring authenticated binds and limiting what each account can read removes anonymous access to user and group data. Moving to LDAPS encrypts the traffic, which protects confidentiality in transit, but anonymous binds would still be accepted, so enumeration remains possible over an encrypted channel. Changing query timeouts barely slows an attacker and does not restrict access. Adding a replica improves availability but duplicates the same permissive configuration on another server.
questions.review_notes: AI-authored original question pending SME review.

questions.question: When an NTP server has legacy monitoring queries enabled and exposed, which information is an attacker most likely to enumerate from it?

citations.source: EC-Council CEH Exam Blueprint v5.0 / CEH v13 brochure
citations.reference: M04 Enumeration (Reconnaissance Techniques)

options.text: The password hashes of the organization's domain user accounts
A list of hosts that recently synchronized with the server
The complete DNS zone of the organization
The encryption keys used by the organization's VPN

questions.justification: Correct Answer: B. Legacy NTP monitoring features can return a list of recent clients, revealing internal host addresses and helping an attacker map the network; the same feature has also been abused for amplification attacks, so it should be disabled or restricted. NTP does not store domain password hashes, which reside in directory databases. A DNS zone is obtained from name servers, for example through misconfigured zone transfers. VPN keys are held by VPN gateways and key management systems, not by time servers.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS)?
questions.domain: System Hacking Phases and Attack Techniques

citations.source: EC-Council CEH Exam Blueprint v5.0 / CEH v13 brochure
citations.reference: M05 Vulnerability Analysis (System Hacking Phases and Attack Techniques)

options.text: Providing a standardized numerical rating of a vulnerability's severity
Cataloging adversary tactics and techniques observed in real attacks
Assigning a unique public identifier to each disclosed vulnerability
Classifying the underlying types of software weaknesses

questions.justification: Correct Answer: A. CVSS produces a score from 0.0 to 10.0 based on characteristics such as attack vector, complexity, privileges required and impact, giving organizations a consistent way to express severity. Assigning unique identifiers to disclosed vulnerabilities is the role of the CVE program. Classifying types of software weaknesses, such as improper input validation, is the purpose of CWE. Cataloging real-world adversary tactics and techniques describes MITRE ATT&CK. All four are related resources, but only CVSS is a severity scoring system.

questions.question: Why do vulnerability assessors often prefer authenticated (credentialed) scans over unauthenticated scans for internal hosts?
questions.domain: System Hacking Phases and Attack Techniques

citations.source: EC-Council CEH Exam Blueprint v5.0 / CEH v13 brochure
citations.reference: M05 Vulnerability Analysis (System Hacking Phases and Attack Techniques)

options.text: They can inspect installed software, patch levels and local settings, producing more accurate results
They remove the need for written authorization from the system owner
They generate no network traffic and are therefore invisible to monitoring tools
They automatically exploit each finding to prove that it is real

questions.justification: Correct Answer: A. With valid credentials the scanner can log in and read installed packages, registry or configuration settings and patch levels, which reveals issues invisible from the network and reduces false positives. Credentialed scans still generate network traffic and are normally visible to monitoring. Any scan, authenticated or not, requires written authorization from the asset owner; credentials do not replace permission. Vulnerability scanners identify and report weaknesses; they do not automatically exploit findings, which would be penetration testing and carry operational risk.

questions.question: A vulnerability scanner reports a critical flaw specific to one web server product on a host that, after manual verification, is confirmed to run an entirely different web server product that is not affected. How should this finding be classified?
questions.domain: System Hacking Phases and Attack Techniques

citations.source: EC-Council CEH Exam Blueprint v5.0 / CEH v13 brochure
citations.reference: M05 Vulnerability Analysis (System Hacking Phases and Attack Techniques)

options.text: True negative
False positive
False negative
True positive

questions.justification: Correct Answer: B. A false positive occurs when a tool reports a vulnerability that does not actually exist, here because the scanner misidentified the product. Manual validation of findings is an important step before reporting. A false negative is the opposite error: a real vulnerability that the scanner fails to report, which is usually more dangerous because it gives false assurance. A true positive would mean the reported vulnerability is real. A true negative means the scanner correctly reports that no vulnerability exists, which is not the case since an alert was raised.

questions.question: After the operations team reports that patches were deployed, the security team rescans the affected hosts and compares the results with the original findings before closing the tickets. Which vulnerability management life cycle activity is this?
questions.domain: System Hacking Phases and Attack Techniques

citations.source: EC-Council CEH Exam Blueprint v5.0 / CEH v13 brochure
citations.reference: M05 Vulnerability Analysis (System Hacking Phases and Attack Techniques)

options.text: Remediation
Risk assessment
Verification
Creating a baseline

questions.justification: Correct Answer: C. Verification confirms that remediation actions were actually applied and effective, typically by rescanning or retesting and comparing against the original findings; only then are items closed. Risk assessment happens earlier, when findings are analyzed and prioritized according to impact and likelihood. Creating a baseline is part of pre-assessment, when assets are identified and their business value is understood. Remediation is the act of fixing, patching or mitigating the vulnerabilities, which the operations team already performed before the rescan took place.

questions.question: An assessment finds a vulnerability with a CVSS base score of 9.8 on an isolated lab host that is not reachable from any network, and one scored 7.5 on an internet-facing payment server that is being actively exploited in the wild. How should remediation be prioritized?
questions.domain: System Hacking Phases and Attack Techniques

citations.source: EC-Council CEH Exam Blueprint v5.0 / CEH v13 brochure
citations.reference: M05 Vulnerability Analysis (System Hacking Phases and Attack Techniques)

options.text: Fix whichever vulnerability was published earliest, regardless of the asset
Prioritize by risk context, fixing the internet-facing payment server first
Defer both until the next scheduled maintenance window to avoid disruption
Always follow the CVSS base score, fixing the lab host first

questions.justification: Correct Answer: B. The CVSS base score describes intrinsic severity but ignores the environment. Effective prioritization combines severity with exposure, business criticality and threat intelligence such as known active exploitation. An internet-facing payment system under active attack carries far higher risk than an isolated lab machine. Following the base score alone ignores this context. Publication date says nothing about current risk to the organization. Deferring both leaves an actively exploited, business-critical system exposed, which is unacceptable when the threat is already present.

questions.question: Which technique hides data inside another file, such as an image or audio file, so that the very existence of the secret message is concealed?
questions.domain: System Hacking Phases and Attack Techniques

citations.source: EC-Council CEH Exam Blueprint v5.0 / CEH v13 brochure
citations.reference: M06 System Hacking (System Hacking Phases and Attack Techniques)

options.text: Steganography
Encryption
Hashing
Compression

questions.justification: Correct Answer: A. Steganography conceals the presence of information by embedding it in an innocent-looking carrier such as an image, audio or video file. Attackers may use it to hide data or tools, and defenders use steganalysis to detect it. Encryption protects the confidentiality of content, but ciphertext is visibly present and obviously protected. Hashing produces a fixed-length digest used for integrity checks and cannot be reversed to recover a hidden message. Compression reduces size and offers no concealment of the fact that data exists.

questions.question: An attacker attempts to authenticate by trying each entry from a precompiled list of common words and leaked passwords. Which type of password attack is this?
questions.domain: System Hacking Phases and Attack Techniques

citations.source: EC-Council CEH Exam Blueprint v5.0 / CEH v13 brochure
citations.reference: M06 System Hacking (System Hacking Phases and Attack Techniques)

options.text: Keylogging
Rainbow table attack
Dictionary attack
Brute-force attack

questions.justification: Correct Answer: C. A dictionary attack tests candidate passwords drawn from a wordlist of common words and previously leaked passwords, exploiting the tendency of users to choose predictable passwords. A brute-force attack tries every possible combination of characters within a given length and character set, without relying on a list. A rainbow table attack uses precomputed hash chains to reverse unsalted hashes, rather than attempting logins. Keylogging captures keystrokes as the user types, which is a collection technique, not a guessing attack.

questions.question: What type of attack is most directly defeated by adding a unique random salt to each password before hashing it for storage?
questions.domain: System Hacking Phases and Attack Techniques

citations.source: EC-Council CEH Exam Blueprint v5.0 / CEH v13 brochure
citations.reference: M06 System Hacking (System Hacking Phases and Attack Techniques)

options.text: Shoulder surfing while the password is typed
Phishing pages that capture credentials
Keystroke logging on the user's workstation
Precomputed hash (rainbow table) attacks

questions.justification: Correct Answer: D. A unique salt means that identical passwords produce different hashes, so tables of hashes precomputed for common passwords become useless and each hash must be attacked individually. Salting protects stored hashes only. A keylogger captures the password as it is typed, before any hashing occurs. Shoulder surfing observes the password visually, which no storage mechanism can prevent. Phishing tricks users into submitting their plaintext credentials to an attacker. These threats require controls such as endpoint protection, awareness and multi-factor authentication.
questions.review_notes: AI-authored original question pending SME review.

questions.question: Authentication logs show one failed login attempt against each of several hundred different accounts within a few minutes, all from the same source and all using the same common password, staying below the lockout threshold. Which attack is most likely taking place?
questions.domain: System Hacking Phases and Attack Techniques

citations.source: EC-Council CEH Exam Blueprint v5.0 / CEH v13 brochure
citations.reference: M06 System Hacking (System Hacking Phases and Attack Techniques)

options.text: Dictionary attack against a single account
Pass-the-hash
Credential stuffing with unique leaked pairs
Password spraying

questions.justification: Correct Answer: D. Password spraying tries one or a few common passwords against many accounts, keeping attempts per account low to avoid lockouts. The pattern of many accounts with the same password from one source matches it exactly. A dictionary attack against a single account would show many attempts on one username. Pass-the-hash reuses captured hashes to authenticate and does not produce failed guesses of a common password. Untrusted input is concatenated into queries as executable code

questions.question: Which practice best protects IoT devices against the installation of malicious firmware?
questions.domain: Mobile Platform, IoT, and OT Hacking

citations.source: EC-Council CEH Exam Blueprint v5.0 / CEH v13 brochure
citations.reference: M18 IoT and OT Hacking (Mobile Platform, IoT, and OT Hacking)

options.text: Accepting firmware updates from any source over unencrypted HTTP
Hiding the firmware download URL from the public
Signed firmware verified by the device before installation and boot
Disabling firmware updates entirely after deployment

questions.justification: Correct Answer: C. Code signing combined with secure boot ensures that a device only installs and runs firmware produced by the legitimate vendor, because any modification invalidates the signature. Accepting updates from any source over plain HTTP invites tampering and malicious updates. Disabling updates prevents malicious firmware in theory, but leaves every discovered vulnerability permanently unpatched, which is a greater risk. Hiding the download URL is security through obscurity: once the location is found or firmware is intercepted, nothing prevents an attacker from supplying a modified image.

questions.question: A plant relies on legacy controllers that use an industrial protocol with no authentication, and they cannot be patched or replaced for several years. Which compensating control is most appropriate?
questions.domain: Mobile Platform, IoT, and OT Hacking

citations.source: EC-Council CEH Exam Blueprint v5.0 / CEH v13 brochure
citations.reference: M18 IoT and OT Hacking (Mobile Platform, IoT, and OT Hacking)

options.text: Install standard endpoint antivirus agents directly on the controllers
Segmentation with an industrial firewall allowing only authorized hosts and commands
Run frequent aggressive active vulnerability scans against the live controllers
Expose the controllers to the internet so the vendor can support them directly

questions.justification: Correct Answer: B. When devices cannot authenticate commands or be patched, the risk is reduced by controlling who can talk to them: strict segmentation, protocol-aware filtering that allows only authorized engineering stations and operations, and passive network monitoring to detect anomalies without disturbing the process. Controllers usually cannot run standard antivirus agents, and doing so could affect real-time operation. Aggressive active scanning can crash fragile OT devices and disrupt production. Direct internet exposure makes unauthenticated devices reachable by anyone, greatly increasing the risk.

questions.question: Under the cloud shared responsibility model for infrastructure as a service (IaaS), who is typically responsible for patching the guest operating system of a virtual machine?

citations.source: EC-Council CEH Exam Blueprint v5.0 / CEH v13 brochure
citations.reference: M19 Cloud Computing (Cloud Computing)

options.text: The server hardware manufacturer
The cloud service provider
The customer's internet service provider
The cloud customer

questions.justification: Correct Answer: D. In IaaS, the provider secures the physical data centers, hardware, network and virtualization layer, while the customer manages everything installed on top: the guest operating system, applications, data, identities and configurations. Patching the guest OS is therefore the customer's job. The provider takes on more of this responsibility in PaaS and SaaS models, where it manages the operating system. The hardware manufacturer supplies equipment to the provider and has no role in customer VMs. The internet service provider only delivers connectivity.

questions.question: A development team uploads individual functions that run only when triggered by events, while the provider manages the servers, runtime and automatic scaling. Which cloud computing model is this?

citations.source: EC-Council CEH Exam Blueprint v5.0 / CEH v13 brochure
citations.reference: M19 Cloud Computing (Cloud Computing)

options.text: Colocation hosting
On-premises server virtualization
Serverless computing (FaaS)
Infrastructure as a service

questions.justification: Correct Answer: C. In serverless computing, or function as a service, developers deploy code as event-driven functions and the provider handles servers, runtime, scaling and billing per execution. Security focus shifts to function permissions, dependencies, event input validation and configuration. With infrastructure as a service, the customer manages virtual machines and their operating systems. On-premises virtualization runs on the organization's own hardware, managed internally. Colocation rents data center space, power and connectivity for the customer's own servers, without managing any runtime for them.

questions.question: A cloud security review finds an object storage bucket containing customer records that is readable by anyone on the internet. Which action best addresses both this finding and similar future exposures?

citations.source: EC-Council CEH Exam Blueprint v5.0 / CEH v13 brochure
citations.reference: M19 Cloud Computing (Cloud Computing)

options.text: Move the bucket to a different geographic region with stricter laws
Block public access, apply least-privilege policies and monitor posture continuously
Enable object versioning so that any deleted records can be restored
Rename the bucket to a long, random and hard-to-guess name

questions.justification: Correct Answer: B. Publicly accessible storage is one of the most common causes of cloud data exposure. Blocking public access and applying least-privilege policies fixes the immediate problem, and cloud security posture management continuously detects similar misconfigurations. Versioning helps recover from deletion or overwriting, but it does not restrict who can read the data. A random name is obscurity; discovery techniques and leaked links still reveal the bucket. Changing the region affects latency and data residency, not the public access setting.

questions.question: Which practice most reduces the risk that a compromised container can be used to take control of its host?

citations.source: EC-Council CEH Exam Blueprint v5.0 / CEH v13 brochure
citations.reference: M19 Cloud Computing (Cloud Computing)

options.text: Always pull the latest image tag without scanning it first
Run as non-root with minimal capabilities, no privileged mode, patched host kernel
Share the host's process and network namespaces with each container
Run containers in privileged mode to avoid permission errors at runtime

questions.justification: Correct Answer: B. Containers share the host kernel, so isolation depends on namespaces, capabilities and kernel security. Running as a non-root user, dropping unnecessary capabilities, avoiding privileged mode and patching the host kernel all shrink the paths for container escape. Privileged mode grants the container near-host-level access, which makes escape trivial. Sharing host namespaces removes isolation boundaries. Pulling unscanned images, especially a floating latest tag, can introduce vulnerable or malicious software and also reduces reproducibility; image scanning and pinned, trusted images are the safer practice.

questions.question: A web application running on a cloud virtual machine has a server-side request forgery flaw that could let attackers reach the instance metadata service and obtain temporary credentials. Which combination of measures best mitigates this risk?

citations.source: EC-Council CEH Exam Blueprint v5.0 / CEH v13 brochure
citations.reference: M19 Cloud Computing (Cloud Computing)

options.text: Rotate the SSH keys used by administrators to access the VM
Move the application to a larger instance type with more memory
Enable full-disk encryption on the virtual machine's storage volumes
Fix the SSRF, require token-based metadata access and use a least-privilege role

questions.justification: Correct Answer: D. Metadata services can hand out credentials for the role attached to an instance, so an SSRF flaw can become a cloud account compromise. Fixing the flaw removes the entry point, token-based metadata access blocks simple forged requests, and a least-privilege role limits what stolen credentials can do. Disk encryption protects data at rest, not credentials obtained through requests. A larger instance type changes performance only. Rotating administrators' SSH keys does not affect temporary role credentials issued by the metadata service.

questions.question: Which of the following is a symmetric encryption algorithm?

citations.source: EC-Council CEH Exam Blueprint v5.0 / CEH v13 brochure
citations.reference: M20 Cryptography (Cryptography)

options.text: Elliptic curve cryptography (ECC)
AES
RSA
Diffie-Hellman

questions.justification: Correct Answer: B. AES is a symmetric block cipher: the same secret key is used to encrypt and decrypt, which makes it fast and suitable for bulk data encryption. RSA is an asymmetric algorithm based on a public and private key pair, used for key exchange and digital signatures. Elliptic curve cryptography is an asymmetric approach that offers strong security with shorter keys. Diffie-Hellman is an asymmetric key agreement protocol that lets two parties derive a shared secret, which is then typically used with a symmetric cipher such as AES.

questions.question: A user compares the SHA-256 digest of a downloaded file with the value published by the vendor. Which security property is being verified?

citations.source: EC-Council CEH Exam Blueprint v5.0 / CEH v13 brochure
citations.reference: M20 Cryptography (Cryptography)

options.text: Integrity
Availability
Confidentiality
Anonymity

questions.justification: Correct Answer: A. A cryptographic hash produces a digest that changes completely if even one bit of the input changes. Matching digests show that the file was not altered or corrupted, which verifies integrity; to also confirm origin, the published digest must come from a trusted, authenticated source or be digitally signed. Hashing does not provide confidentiality, because the file itself remains readable. Availability concerns whether systems and data are accessible when needed. Anonymity relates to hiding identity and is not a property checked by comparing hashes.

questions.question: Alice digitally signs a message and sends it to Bob. Which key does Bob use to verify the signature?

citations.source: EC-Council CEH Exam Blueprint v5.0 / CEH v13 brochure
citations.reference: M20 Cryptography (Cryptography)

options.text: Alice's public key
Alice's private key
Bob's public key
Bob's private key

questions.justification: Correct Answer: A. A digital signature is created with the signer's private key, which only the signer holds, and verified with the signer's public key, which anyone can obtain, typically from a certificate. Therefore Bob uses Alice's public key. Alice's private key must never be shared, and it is used to create the signature, not to verify it. Bob's private key is used to decrypt messages encrypted for Bob or to sign his own messages. Bob's public key is used by others to encrypt data for him, not to verify Alice's signature.

questions.question: A web server's private key is compromised months before its certificate expires. How do relying parties learn that the certificate should no longer be trusted?

citations.source: EC-Council CEH Exam Blueprint v5.0 / CEH v13 brochure
citations.reference: M20 Cryptography (Cryptography)

options.text: Clients keep trusting it until the expiration date is reached
The certificate automatically switches to a new public key
The registration authority re-issues the same certificate with a new serial number
The CA revokes the certificate, and clients check its status through a CRL or OCSP

questions.justification: Correct Answer: D. When a private key is compromised, the certificate must be revoked by the issuing certificate authority. Relying parties learn about revocation by consulting a certificate revocation list or querying an OCSP responder, sometimes via OCSP stapling. Continuing to trust the certificate until expiration would let an attacker impersonate the server for months. Certificates are signed, static documents and cannot change their public key. A registration authority verifies identities for the CA and does not re-issue the same compromised key under a new serial number as a fix.

questions.question: Which property ensures that if a server's long-term private key is stolen, previously recorded encrypted sessions still cannot be decrypted?

citations.source: EC-Council CEH Exam Blueprint v5.0 / CEH v13 brochure
citations.reference: M20 Cryptography (Cryptography)

options.text: Key stretching
Perfect forward secrecy
Key escrow
Non-repudiation

questions.justification: Correct Answer: B. Perfect forward secrecy uses ephemeral key exchanges, such as ephemeral Diffie-Hellman, to create unique session keys that are never derivable from the server's long-term private key. Stealing that key later does not reveal keys for recorded past sessions. Key escrow deposits keys with a third party so they can be recovered, which increases exposure rather than protecting past sessions. Non-repudiation ensures that a sender cannot deny having signed a message. Key stretching strengthens weak passwords against guessing by making key derivation slower.
